title: Fix local cached PDF 500 on cloud-backed files
description:
## Context
After pdfv-yg1.15, local cached PDFs opened through extension dynamic rules hit /view?path=... and the daemon re-read the source PDF to compute its content hash. For OneDrive/iCloud-style files, macOS can return OSError [Errno 11] Resource deadlock avoided, producing Internal Server Error.

## What changed
Resolve cached local PDFs from mappings.tsv before falling back to content hashing, so already-cached local PDFs do not need the daemon to read cloud-backed source bytes on open.

## Verification
curl and Browser against the exact failing KTN Pensumbok /view?path URL returned the custom viewer with no Internal Server Error.
close_reason: Completed

title: Portability & robustness hardening: reproducible toolchain, bootstrap, regression safety
description:
## Context

Post-ADR-0011 the viewer runs on a natively-built arm64 pdf2htmlEX, but the architecture review (2026-06-12) found the remaining fragility is concentrated in three places: the toolchain exists only as a one-off copied binary, standing up the system on a fresh Mac is tribal knowledge, and the overlay (90% of all work) has no regression guard. This epic tracks making the system nimble, clean, and robust on this Mac and reproducible on future Macs.

The six loosely-coupled-parts shape (overlay / convert scripts / injector / daemon / extension / Raycast) is correct and must not be restructured. See docs/adr/0011-native-arm64-pdf2htmlex.md and docs/non-goals.md.

## What to build

Child beads cover: Homebrew tap or relocatable artifact for the toolchain, Brewfile, setup.sh bootstrap, doctor.sh diagnostics, committed Playwright smoke test, content-hash overlay versioning, cache provenance metadata, and a parked ES-module split.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All child beads closed or explicitly re-scoped
- [ ] A fresh arm64 Mac can reach a working viewer following only README + scripts

## Verification

Per child bead. Epic-level: walk the bootstrap path on a clean macOS user account and confirm end-to-end conversion + viewing.
close_reason: Hardening epic complete: reproducible toolchain, one-command bootstrap+diagnosis, regression smoke test, self-busting assets, provenance-tagged cache

comments.author: andersbekkevard
comments.text: All eight children closed 2026-06-12. Shipped: tap distribution (andersbekkevard/homebrew-tools + release), Brewfile, doctor.sh, smoke-viewer.sh, setup.sh, content-hash overlay versioning, cache provenance (154 entries), conservative overlay module split. Epic-level fresh-Mac walk on a clean account remains the one untested path (noted in pdfv-6el.5).

title: Publish native pdf2htmlEX as a personal Homebrew tap (or relocatable tarball)
description:
## Context

The production converter (~/.local/opt/pdf2htmlEX) is a one-off artifact: built once in ~/dev/external/pdf2htmlEX_v2/native/build.sh, copied by scripts/install-native-pdf2htmlex.sh, linking Homebrew dylibs at absolute /opt/homebrew/opt/* paths. A brew cleanup, poppler major bump, or new Mac breaks or loses it, and the installer can only copy, never recreate. ADR 0011 records the build provenance.

## What to build

Preferred: a personal Homebrew tap (e.g. andersbekkevard/homebrew-tools) with a pdf2htmlex formula encoding the v2 build recipe (upstream master + poppler 24.06.1 + fontforge 20230101, the CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM/pkg-config/iconv/CoreServices fixes from native/build.sh). brew then owns deps, upgrades, and arm64 builds on any Mac. This would be the first working pdf2htmlEX formula since 2019.

Fallback if formula authoring rabbit-holes: a relocatable tarball — dylibbundler-style @rpath rewrite of the binary + bundled dylibs + share/, attached to a GitHub release on the fork; install-native-pdf2htmlex.sh learns to fetch it.

Update scripts/install-native-pdf2htmlex.sh and ADR 0011 to point at whichever path ships.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Toolchain installable on a machine without ~/dev/external present
- [ ] Survives brew upgrade poppler (rebuild path or bundled deps)
- [ ] scripts/install-native-pdf2htmlex.sh and docs updated
- [ ] Conversion smoke test passes from the new install

## Verification

On this Mac: uninstall ~/.local/opt/pdf2htmlEX, install via the new path, run scripts/install-native-pdf2htmlex.sh self-test or a direct conversion of a fixture PDF, confirm daemon-served output renders.

HITL: user must create the tap repo / GitHub release and decide naming.
close_reason: Shipped via the bead's pragmatic fallback: relocatable bundle + binary-pour formula on andersbekkevard/homebrew-tools + GitHub release; installer falls back to brew keg

title: Add Brewfile declaring runtime dependencies
description:
## Context

Runtime deps (poppler data, cairo, glib, freetype, fontconfig, gettext, jpeg-turbo, libpng, libxml2, openjpeg + pdftocairo/pdfinfo from poppler) are implicit — discoverable only via otool -L and script reading. A Brewfile makes 'what does this machine need' declarative for future Macs.

## What to build

Brewfile at repo root listing the formulas the toolchain links and the scripts invoke. Comment each line with which component needs it. Reference it from README setup section.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] brew bundle check passes on this machine
- [ ] Every /opt/homebrew dylib in otool -L of the binary is owned by a listed formula
- [ ] README references it

## Verification

brew bundle check --file=Brewfile exits 0; cross-check otool -L ~/.local/opt/pdf2htmlEX/bin/pdf2htmlEX against the list.
close_reason: Brewfile shipped: 10 runtime formulas, empirically derived, check green

comments.author: andersbekkevard
comments.text: Verification (audited by orchestrator): brew bundle check --no-upgrade --file=Brewfile → 'dependencies are satisfied', exit 0. 9 dylib formulas map 1:1 to otool -L of the binary (cairo glib gettext freetype libpng jpeg-turbo libxml2 openjpeg fontconfig) + poppler for pdftocairo/pdfinfo/share-data. Orchestrator decisions: --no-upgrade semantics (presence is the contract, not freshness — poppler 26.04 installed vs 26.06 current is fine); uv documented as a comment, not a formula (machine intentionally uses astral standalone; brew copy would shadow-drift). README references the Brewfile.

title: Write scripts/doctor.sh — one-command diagnosis of the full chain
description:
## Context

Most historical debugging sessions (stale overlay assets, daemon down, missing toolchain, broken symlink, formerly Docker-not-running) reduce to checking one link in a known chain. That chain lives in heads and docs, not in a tool. CLAUDE.md 'Logs & debugging' lists the manual commands.

## What to build

scripts/doctor.sh: idempotent, read-only, checks each link and prints one PASS/FAIL line per check with a one-line fix hint:
- daemon /healthz on :7435 (and launchd job loaded)
- ~/.cache/pdf_viewer/_assets symlink resolves into the repo's assets/
- native binary exists + --version reports expected libs
- /opt/homebrew/share/poppler exists; pdftocairo/pdfinfo on PATH (warn-only, optional features)
- every /opt/homebrew dylib in otool -L resolves
- mappings.tsv exists and is writable; cache dir writable
- /_assets/overlay.js?v=current returns 200 through the daemon
- extension probe: a *.pdf URL redirect check if cheaply possible, else print the manual check

Exit non-zero if any required check fails; warnings don't fail.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Detects and names each broken link when artificially induced (daemon stopped, symlink removed, binary moved)
- [ ] Read-only — never mutates state
- [ ] README/CLAUDE.md debugging section points to it

## Verification

Run doctor on healthy system (exit 0); kickstart -k the daemon off / rename the binary / break the symlink one at a time and confirm the failing line names the right component each time. Restore state after.
close_reason: doctor.sh shipped: 11-check read-only chain diagnosis with fix hints, PDF_VIEWER_PORT override for testability

comments.author: andersbekkevard
comments.text: Verification (audited by orchestrator): doctor.sh ran green independently (exit 0, 11 checks). Agent proved induced failures one at a time: binary moved→FAIL names binary; symlink broken→FAIL names _assets; dead port via PDF_VIEWER_PORT=7999→FAIL daemon+overlay.js checks. State restored, final run exit 0, no .bak strays. Read-only by construction. README+CLAUDE.md debugging pointers added.

title: Commit a Playwright viewer smoke test (scripts/smoke-viewer.sh)
description:
## Context

The overlay is where 90% of changes land and where regressions (Cmd-F, navigation, render-loop kill) have repeatedly bitten. The 2026-06-12 migration verification effectively wrote the one test worth keeping; it lives only in a transcript. docs/verification.md doctrine: narrowest real proof — this is one smoke test, not a test pyramid.

## What to build

scripts/smoke-viewer.sh + a small committed fixture (convert a tiny checked-in PDF into a temp cache entry at run time, or keep a checked-in fixture entry). Headless Chromium (reuse the locally-cached Playwright; do not add global tooling) asserting against a daemon-served entry:
- expected .pf page count renders
- overlay booted (#pdf2html-pageno-current present, sidebar DOM)
- pdf2htmlEX render loop killed (defaultViewer.render_timer === null)
- window.find('<known word>') === true
- zero console errors, zero failed /_assets/ requests

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Single command, exits non-zero on any assertion failure
- [ ] Runs against the real daemon on :7435, no mocks
- [ ] Documented in docs/verification.md as the standard pre-close check for overlay beads
- [ ] No new global dependencies

## Verification

Run it green; then deliberately break overlay.js (e.g. comment out killPdf2htmlExRenderLoop), confirm it fails with a pointed message, revert, confirm green.
close_reason: Playwright smoke test shipped: scripts/smoke-viewer.sh + .cjs against real daemon, temp cache entry, trap-cleaned

comments.text: Verification (audited by orchestrator): ran scripts/smoke-viewer.sh independently → PASS exit 0 (~11.5s): 1 .pf page, overlay booted, render_timer===null, find('Normal') true, 0 console errors, 0 failed /_assets/. Agent proved failure detection: commenting killPdf2htmlExRenderLoop call → exit 1 with pointed message; overlay.js restored (verified call site intact at line 17, all remaining diff hunks belong to an unrelated concurrent user edit in mountResumePosition). title: Write scripts/setup.sh — idempotent fresh-Mac bootstrap
description:
## Context

Standing the system up on a fresh Mac is tribal knowledge spread across README, CLAUDE.md, and memory: launchd plist (hardcoded user paths), _assets symlink, toolchain install, brew deps, extension side-load, Raycast script dir. Goal: one command + two documented manual steps.

## What to build

scripts/setup.sh, idempotent:
- brew bundle (Brewfile bead)
- toolchain install via scripts/install-native-pdf2htmlex.sh (or the tap, once pdfv-6el.1 ships)
- template launchd/com.anders.pdf_viewer.plist with the current $HOME and repo path, load via launchctl
- create ~/.cache/pdf_viewer + _assets symlink into the repo
- finish by running scripts/doctor.sh (pdfv-6el.3) as the success gate
- print the two manual steps it cannot do: extension load in Comet, Raycast script-directory add

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Safe to re-run on an already-configured machine (no duplicate launchd jobs, no clobbered symlinks)
- [ ] Plist no longer hardcodes /Users/andersbekkevard (templated at setup time)
- [ ] Ends with doctor.sh green
- [ ] README quick-start reduced to: clone, ./scripts/setup.sh, two manual steps

## Verification

Re-run on this configured Mac (idempotency, exit 0). Strongest proof when feasible: run from a clean macOS user account and confirm a PDF converts and renders end-to-end after the two manual steps.
close_reason: setup.sh shipped: idempotent bootstrap (brew bundle, toolchain, templated launchd plist, symlink) gated on doctor.sh

title: Derive overlay asset version from content hash; drop manual OVERLAY_VERSION
description:
## Context

A recurring bug class ('works after Cmd-Shift-R') is stale overlay assets. The ?v=N query param relies on a human remembering to bump OVERLAY_VERSION in scripts/pdf2html-convert.sh, and cached HTML keeps old N until re-injected. scripts/inject-overlay.py owns tag writing; the daemon serves /_assets/.

## What to build

- inject-overlay.py computes v from a short content hash of assets/overlay.js + overlay.css at injection time (stable across re-runs when files unchanged — keep injection idempotent).
- Daemon serves /_assets/ with ETag and a short max-age so even stale ?v= HTML self-corrects on 304 revalidation.
- Remove the OVERLAY_VERSION constant from all scripts (convert, upgrade-cache); upgrade-cache --mode=inject naturally rewrites old entries to the current hash.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Editing overlay.js then re-injecting changes the v param with no manual bump
- [ ] Re-injecting with unchanged assets is a no-op (idempotency preserved)
- [ ] Old cached entries refresh assets correctly via ETag without re-injection
- [ ] OVERLAY_VERSION constant gone; docs mentioning the bump ritual updated

## Verification

curl -sI localhost:7435/_assets/overlay.js shows ETag; If-None-Match returns 304. Edit a comment in overlay.js, run upgrade-cache --mode=inject on one entry, confirm new v in HTML and browser picks up the change without hard reload.
close_reason: Content-hash overlay versioning shipped: injector derives ?v= from sha256(overlay.js+css), daemon revalidates with ETag+must-revalidate, manual bump ritual deleted

Live daemon serves /_assets with ETag + Cache-Control: max-age=60, must-revalidate; If-None-Match → 304 (verified by orchestrator post-restart). Double-injection byte-identical (cmp); content-change marker test flipped v to b59c500e73 and back. title: Record conversion provenance in each cache entry's meta.json
description:
## Context

The cache is now permanently mixed-provenance: 153 Docker-era entries plus native ones, indistinguishable without forensics. The first time a rendering bug correlates with converter era (e.g. the known WOFF glyph-outline difference, ADR 0011), we'll want to query provenance with one rg. Keep mappings.tsv untouched — greppability is a feature; provenance belongs in per-entry meta.json (docs/cache.md).

## What to build

- scripts/pdf2html-convert.sh (and the indexers/reconvert path) write converter provenance after a successful conversion: converter (native-arm64), pdf2htmlEX version, poppler version, conversion date, overlay version at injection. Decide placement: extend extract-pdf-meta.sh's meta.json or a sibling provenance key written by the convert script — keep pdfinfo-derived fields and pipeline-derived fields clearly separated.
- One-shot backfill marking all pre-2026-06-12 entries converter=docker-amd64 (date-based, documented heuristic).
- Document the schema in docs/cache.md.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Fresh conversion writes provenance; reconvert overwrites it
- [ ] Backfill marks legacy entries without touching their HTML
- [ ] docs/cache.md documents the fields
- [ ] rg over the cache answers 'which entries are Docker-era' in one command

## Verification

Convert an uncached PDF, cat its meta.json. Run backfill, spot-check a known legacy entry (e.g. 00bf2159e2abff16) and confirm docker provenance + untouched HTML mtime.
close_reason: Provenance shipped: pipeline writes provenance object on convert; 154 entries backfilled; merge-safe with pdfinfo writer

Merge-safety both directions proven by agent (provenance survives extract-pdf-meta.sh re-run byte-identical; pdfinfo fields survive provenance write). HTML mtimes unchanged on spot-checked entries. Fresh-convert test entry showed full provenance object (converter/pdf2htmlex/poppler/converted_at/overlay_version), test entry + shim cleaned, dangling mappings.tsv row removed by orchestrator (149 rows, verified). bash -n all green. docs/cache.md schema section added.

title: Split overlay.js into native ES modules (parked until growth demands it)
description:
## Context

overlay.js is ~2.5-3k LoC in one file. The zero-build-step property is a core architecture feature (live-served via symlink, ⌘⇧R reload) and must be preserved. Below ~4k LoC a split is not worth the churn; this bead exists so the eventual split is planned, not improvised.

## What to build

When overlay.js growth makes navigation painful: split into native ES modules (type=module script tag, no bundler) along existing seams — keybindings/palette, navigation/scroll, search/selection, sidebar/outline, pins, boot/render-loop-kill. inject-overlay.py updates the script tag; cache-busting must cover all modules (compose with pdfv-6el.6's content-hash versioning).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No build step introduced; ⌘⇧R live-edit workflow unchanged
- [ ] Module boundaries follow the seams above, no behavior change
- [ ] Smoke test (pdfv-6el.4) green before and after
- [ ] docs updated where they reference 'the overlay.js file'

## Verification

scripts/smoke-viewer.sh green; manual pass over keybindings per docs/keybindings.md in a real converted PDF.

HITL: user judgement on when growth justifies it and on module boundaries.
close_reason: Conservative ES-module split shipped: finger seam extracted, entry stays type=module, per-module busting via ETag revalidation; tangled core honestly left whole

title: Detect scanned (text-less) PDFs at conversion and surface a notice
description:
## Context

Scanned PDFs have no text layer, so pdf2htmlEX converts them to pure page images. Everything the project exists for — native Cmd-F search, text selection, Vimium hinting, and the future selection-into-LLM-context flow (pdfv-yg1.16) — silently breaks. Today there is no detection: the conversion succeeds and the user discovers the breakage only when search/selection mysteriously does nothing.

## What to build

1. In scripts/pdf2html-convert.sh (and scripts/index-directory.sh if it shares the path), detect text-less PDFs at conversion time — e.g. pdftotext output is empty/near-empty across sampled pages.
2. Still convert (pixel-faithful viewing is fine), but record the 'scanned' flag (e.g. in meta.json next to the cached HTML).
3. Overlay reads the flag and shows a visible, dismissible notice: 'Scanned PDF — no text layer. Search and selection unavailable.'
4. Document text-native PDFs as the supported scope (docs/non-goals.md or docs/cache.md).

Out of scope (park as future work): an ocrmypdf preprocessing pass that bolts a text layer onto detected scans before conversion. Detection + honest notice first; OCR is the known, documented improvement path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Converting a scanned PDF produces a cached entry flagged as text-less
- [ ] Viewer shows a clear notice for flagged documents; text-native PDFs are unaffected
- [ ] Detection adds negligible time to conversion of normal PDFs
- [ ] Supported-scope limitation documented

## Verification

Convert one scanned PDF and one text-native PDF; confirm the notice appears only on the scanned one and that normal conversion behavior is unchanged. Record commands and a screenshot per docs/verification.md.

title: Resume-position lost on reload after outline navigation (stale #pfN hash) + debounce gap
description:
## Context

mountResumePosition (assets/overlay.js, ~line 4034) saves the current page per-document to localStorage (debounced 400ms) and restores it on load — but only when location.hash is empty. Outline navigation calls replaceHash(), which writes #pfN into the URL via history.replaceState and never clears it. The combination loses the user's reading position on a routine flow.

## Verified repro (headless Chromium via Playwright, doc 19f1998aa6212b01 'Attention Is All You Need', 2026-06-12)

**Bug 1 — stale hash discards and clobbers the saved position:**
1. Open doc, navigate via outline to page 3 (URL becomes …#pf3), read on to page 8. Saved = {page: 8}.
2. Reload. Restore is skipped because location.hash is set. Viewer lands at the TOP of the document (pf3 top = 2885px, pf8 top = 10040px after reload — neither the outline target nor the reading position; the browser's own #pf3 anchoring doesn't hold either).
3. ~1s later the debounced writer overwrites saved position: {page: 8} → {page: 1}. The position is permanently lost — subsequent hash-free opens restore nothing.

Same clobber occurs for any non-restoring load (e.g. unknown #hash): landing on page 1 overwrites the saved page after 400ms.

**Bug 2 — debounce gap on rapid close/reopen:**
Scroll to page 9, reload within ~100ms (< 400ms debounce): the page-9 write never lands; saved stays at the previous value. Last movement before a quick close is lost.

**Confirmed working:** plain scroll → wait > 400ms → reload restores exactly (pf5 rect.top identical before/after, 359.5px).

## Suggested fix directions

- Keep hash and saved position from fighting: on page-change, either strip/refresh the #pfN hash (history.replaceState) once the user scrolls away from the outline target, or make mountResumePosition prefer the saved position when its ts is fresher than the hash navigation.
- Don't clobber on non-restoring loads: skip the first write (or compare against saved) when restore was bypassed due to a hash.
- Flush the debounced write on pagehide/visibilitychange to close the rapid-close gap.

## Verification

Repro scripts from the investigation: /tmp/verify_resume_position.py, /tmp/verify_clobber.py, /tmp/verify_stale_hash.py (Playwright, run with: uv run --with playwright python <script>). After the fix, all three flows should restore to the last-read page and the saved value must never regress to page 1 on a hash load.
close_reason: Fixed and verified: stale-hash position loss, page-1 clobber, and debounce gap all resolved in assets/overlay.js

comments.author: andersbekkevard

title: Run AI production experiment
description:
## Context

Parent tracker for evolving pdf_viewer through mostly hands-off agent work on experimental branches while keeping main as the stable baseline.

## What to build

Coordinate the experiment through Beads, repo-owned docs, and narrow agent-ready slices.

## Acceptance criteria

## Verification

Run br ready and confirm child beads are independently actionable.

title: Reproduce and fix Cmd-F failure on large sections
description:
## Context

Native Cmd-F is unreliable on large converted PDFs. The user reports several failure modes: sometimes Cmd-F cannot find text until a hard reload (Cmd-Shift-R), sometimes it finds too many or wrong entries, and pressing Enter can move to an adjacent page without the expected highlighted text visible. TODO.md also says Cmd-F works for small sections but not large sections. ADR 0009 says full-document native find depends on .pf content-visibility: auto and avoiding display:none page gating.

## What to build

Reproduce the native-find failure on a large cached or freshly converted PDF, identify whether the cause is stale injected assets, content-visibility behavior, text-layer ordering, page virtualization, browser find interaction, or reload/cache state, and restore reliable native Cmd-F over large PDFs. Preserve the content-visibility architecture unless evidence requires a new ADR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A large cached or freshly converted PDF reproduces at least one reported failure mode before the fix
- [ ] Cmd-F can find text beyond the initially visible/small section after the fix
- [ ] Enter/cycling in browser find scrolls to a visible native highlight, not an adjacent blank/wrong page
- [ ] The fix does not reintroduce display:none text gating or the deleted surrogate shadow text layer
- [ ] docs/keybindings.md or ADR notes are updated if behavior or architecture changes

## Verification

Use the real daemon at localhost:7435 with a large converted PDF. Verify native Cmd-F finds terms outside the initially visible pages, survives normal reload state, and does not require Cmd-Shift-R to start working.

title: Fix visual-mode next-page navigation when j/k fails but repeated w works
description:
## Context

In visual mode, the user sometimes has to press w repeatedly to advance while j/k does not move to the next page. This breaks the expected vertical reading/navigation model.

## What to build

Find why visual-mode j/k cannot cross certain page/text-layer boundaries and make vertical movement advance predictably to the next logical line/page.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reproduce a case where w w w advances but j j j does not
- [ ] j/k can move through the same boundary without getting stuck
- [ ] The fix respects text ordering and does not create jumps to unrelated figure/caption layers

## Verification

On a converted PDF with the failure mode, enter visual mode and verify j/k can move through the problematic boundary.

title: Decide the minimum ergonomic pins interaction
description:
## Context

Pins/markers are one of the most important product directions. The user wants to drop a location, keep working, jump back quickly, and open a nimble overview of all pins. The design should reference docs/pins.md.

## What to build

Turn docs/pins.md into a concrete first-version interaction contract: terminology, commands, menu shape, ordering, persistence scope, and how it relates to Vimium marks. This is a HITL design bead, not an implementation bead.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] docs/pins.md is updated with the chosen MVP interaction
- [ ] The first version defines how to drop a pin, jump to the latest pin, list pins, and title pins from selected text
- [ ] The design decides whether persistence is in-tab only or cross-session for V1
- [ ] The design decides whether pins use letters, numbers, recency, or explicit names
- [ ] Follow-up implementation beads are updated if the chosen design changes them

## Verification

User reviews docs/pins.md and confirms the MVP interaction before implementation starts.

title: Implement MVP pin drop and jump-back flow
description:
## Context

After the pins interaction is decided in docs/pins.md, implement the smallest useful flow: drop a pin at the current reading location and jump back to it quickly.

## What to build

Implement the chosen V1 from docs/pins.md for dropping a pin and returning to the most recent or selected pin. Keep the implementation easy to revise after user testing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can drop a pin at the current page/viewport anchor
- [ ] If text is selected and the design says to use it, that text becomes the default pin title
- [ ] A user can jump back to the most recent/current pin with the chosen command
- [ ] No undocumented keybinding conflicts are introduced
- [ ] docs/keybindings.md and docs/pins.md are updated

## Verification

Open a converted PDF, drop a pin, move elsewhere, use the chosen command to jump back, and confirm the viewport returns to the pinned location.

title: Implement keyboard-first pins overview
description:
## Context

The user wants a nimble overview of all pins with page number, chapter, quote/title, and possibly a page thumbnail. This should follow the decided interaction in docs/pins.md.

## What to build

Add the chosen pins overview/menu. It should be keyboard-navigable, semantic/Vimium-hintable, and optimized for recognizing and jumping to pins quickly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The overview lists all pins for the current document
- [ ] Each row shows page number and title/quote; chapter is shown when available
- [ ] Keyboard navigation and Enter selection work
- [ ] Controls are real buttons or otherwise Vimium-hintable
- [ ] docs/pins.md documents the final V1 overview behavior

## Verification

Create multiple pins, open the overview, navigate between rows by keyboard, and jump to each pin.

title: Implement homepage search index for all cached PDFs
description:
## Context

The user wants a single shortcut target: a pretty, minimal homepage/search index for the PDF viewer, not itself a PDF, showing all/recent PDFs and a Command-K-like navigation experience. This overlaps with the existing daemon /library and visit tracking.

## What to build

Add a daemon-served homepage/index page that lists recent/cached PDFs and supports fast keyboard search/open. Use the existing visual language where possible and keep it minimal and clean.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A stable URL opens the PDF viewer homepage/index without requiring a PDF path
- [ ] The page lists recently used and/or cached PDFs from existing daemon/library data
- [ ] Search/filter is keyboard-first and can open a selected PDF
- [ ] The page is suitable for mapping to a browser/app shortcut
- [ ] README.md documents the homepage URL and shortcut use

## Verification

Start or use the real daemon, open the homepage URL, search for a known cached PDF, press Enter, and land in that PDF viewer page.

title: Add a native-PDF fallback command
description:
## Context

When text rendering is bad, the user wants an easy toggle/key/palette command to open the same PDF natively instead of deleting cache entries or using hard reload workarounds. The viewer already has passthrough behavior for cache misses and stores source data for some conversions.

## What to build

Add an explicit command that opens the current PDF in the browser/native PDF viewer or original source. Audit whether every cached entry has enough original path/URL/source PDF information; if not, add the smallest source-metadata/copy behavior needed for reliable fallback.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The current viewer exposes a command/palette entry to open the native PDF
- [ ] Local PDFs and remote cached PDFs both have a defined fallback behavior
- [ ] The command does not require deleting cache entries
- [ ] Redirect loops are avoided using the existing passthrough mechanism or an equivalent safe marker
- [ ] docs/keybindings.md and docs/cache.md are updated if commands/cache semantics change

## Verification

Open a cached converted PDF, trigger the native fallback command, and confirm the browser opens the corresponding native PDF surface instead of the custom HTML viewer.

title: Research Comet LLM access to viewer context
description:
## Context

The north star is a PDF viewer optimized for LLM context. Comet has an LLM sidebar that can inspect or fetch some text from pages. We need to know what it can access from the converted viewer and whether the viewer should expose an llms.txt-like layer, current viewport endpoint, or full-document text endpoint.

**Interaction model (north-star framing):** the target UX is Cursor's Cmd-L — select a region of the PDF, hit a key, and that selection (plus page/viewport context) lands in the LLM's context. The key insight: an LLM that merely fetches raw PDF text is fundamentally worse than a viewer that shares *interaction state* — what the user has selected, what page they're on, what they're looking at right now. Without that bridge there is no interaction between the model and the viewer, only blind document retrieval. This is also the strongest demo for the broader 'PDF as first-class surface for an AI assistant' story.

## What to build

Run a focused investigation of what the Comet LLM sidebar can see from the viewer: DOM text, selected text, current viewport, same-origin daemon endpoints, and linked resources. Then propose the smallest context surface that gives the LLM both the whole document and an ergonomic take on what the user is seeing now — with selection-to-context (Cmd-L style) as the priority interaction to enable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Document what Comet LLM can and cannot access from a served PDF viewer page
- [ ] Determine whether it can fetch additional localhost URLs linked from the page
- [ ] Propose whether to expose full-document text, current viewport text, selected text, and/or llms.txt-style metadata
- [ ] Specifically assess feasibility of a Cmd-L-style 'selection into model context' flow and what viewer-side surface it needs
- [ ] Identify privacy/localhost constraints and failure modes
- [ ] Create follow-up implementation beads if the proposed surface is accepted

## Verification

Use a real converted PDF in Comet and record observed LLM sidebar behavior, including exact prompts or tests used.

title: Profile and reduce memory use for large books
description:
## Context

Opening a large book can consume around 2 GB of memory in the browser tab, which is not feasible as a normal reading workflow. Possible causes include pdf2htmlEX image layers, page rendering, content-visibility behavior, retained thumbnails, or asset caching.

## What to build

Measure memory use on a representative large cached book, identify the dominant contributors, and implement the smallest safe reduction. Preserve native find and text selection unless a documented tradeoff is explicitly accepted.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Establish a repeatable before/after memory measurement method
- [ ] Identify the main memory contributors for a large book
- [ ] Reduce memory usage meaningfully or document why the first safe reduction is blocked
- [ ] Native Cmd-F and text selection still work after the change
- [ ] Any architectural tradeoff is captured in docs/adr/ or a follow-up bead

## Verification

Open the same large cached book before and after the change and compare browser tab memory using the chosen repeatable measurement method.

title: Normalize logical text order for search and visual navigation
description:
## Context

pdf2htmlEX text layers can be ordered illogically. Vimium-style navigation, overlay search, and visual-mode j/k can jump up/down when figure or diagram text appears in a different layer/order than the visual reading order. Forking pdf2htmlEX is a future track; first investigate what can be fixed in this repo.

## What to build

Research and prototype a repo-local way to derive visual/logical text order from positions instead of raw DOM order. Apply it only where it improves overlay search/selection/navigation without breaking native browser find.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Identify at least one PDF/page where current order jumps illogically
- [ ] Document whether the fix belongs in overlay code, injection/post-processing, or future pdf2htmlEX work
- [ ] Prototype or implement a narrow order-normalization path for overlay-controlled features
- [ ] Native browser find is not regressed

## Verification

On the repro PDF, use overlay search or visual j/k before and after; confirm movement follows visual reading order better.

title: Show only top-level chapters in header and make sidebar hierarchy navigable
description:
## Context

When a PDF has several layers of chapters, the header should prefer top-level chapters. The left menu should behave more like a collapsible hierarchy so lower-level entries are available without overwhelming the main chapter signal.

## What to build

Adjust outline/chapter presentation so the header uses top-level chapter context, while the sidebar can show nested chapters with collapse/expand behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Header/current chapter display prefers top-level outline entries when nesting exists
- [ ] Sidebar preserves access to nested entries
- [ ] Nested groups can be collapsed/expanded by keyboard and pointer
- [ ] Outline controls remain semantic/Vimium-hintable
- [ ] docs/keybindings.md is updated if new commands are added

## Verification

Open a PDF with nested outline entries and confirm the header shows top-level context while the sidebar supports navigating nested entries.

title: Polish keybinding hint icon styling and Cmd-K copy
description:
## Context

The small icons for keybinds should be slightly darker/more anonymous. The Command-K UI copy should also remove the em dash. This is a narrow visual/text polish task.

## What to build

Adjust the keybinding icon styling by a small amount toward darker grey and remove the em dash from the Command-K copy. Keep the UI quiet and consistent with the existing viewer style.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Keybinding icons render darker/more anonymous without becoming too low-contrast
- [ ] The Command-K surface no longer uses an em dash in the targeted copy
- [ ] No unrelated palette text is rewritten

## Verification

Open the relevant overlay/palette UI and visually confirm the keybinding icons and Command-K copy.

title: Hide page-number Command-K action when unsupported
description:
## Context

The Command-K page-number action should not appear for documents where page numbers are not supported or cannot be mapped correctly. Unsupported commands create dead ends in the palette.

## What to build

Detect whether page-number navigation is supported for the current document and hide or disable the Command-K page-number action when it is not valid. Prefer hiding unless the UI has a clear disabled-state convention.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Documents without supported page-number mapping do not show a usable page-number command
- [ ] Documents with supported page-number mapping still show and execute the command
- [ ] The condition is based on document capability, not a hardcoded filename

## Verification

Open one document with page-number support and one without, then compare Command-K results.

title: Add navigation undo for accidental movement
description:
## Context

The user wants a Cmd-Z-style way to revert accidental movement. This should restore recent viewport/page movement, not undo text edits. It is especially useful when find/selection/navigation unexpectedly moves the reader.

## What to build

Add a small navigation history stack and a command to return to the previous reading position. Choose the key/palette shape according to docs/keybindings.md constraints.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The viewer records meaningful reading-position changes without recording every tiny scroll tick
- [ ] The user can invoke a command to return to the previous position
- [ ] The command does not conflict with browser text-edit undo in input fields
- [ ] docs/keybindings.md documents the command if a keybinding is added

## Verification

Navigate several pages away, invoke the undo movement command, and confirm the viewport returns to the previous meaningful reading position.

title: Make more overlay controls Vimium-hintable
description:
## Context

The note "Make fingers select more things" points at Vimium F hints and clickable/selectable controls. Custom interactive controls must be real buttons or semantic elements to be discoverable.

## What to build

Audit overlay controls and document affordances that should be reachable through Vimium hints. Convert non-semantic clickable divs to buttons or add appropriate role/tabindex only where a native element is not viable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Important overlay controls are reachable through Vimium F hints
- [ ] No inert decorative elements become noisy hint targets
- [ ] Keyboard/focus behavior remains coherent
- [ ] CLAUDE.md guidance remains accurate

## Verification

Open a converted PDF with Vimium enabled, press F, and confirm expected overlay controls receive hints.

title: Investigate KTN page-number discrepancy around Internet pages
description:
## Context

The notes mention a specific discrepancy: 1063 vs 1073 for "Internet" in KTN pensumbok. This likely relates to PDF page index vs printed page number mapping, outline entries, or extracted text positions.

## What to build

Find the relevant cached/local KTN PDF if available, reproduce the discrepancy, and determine whether it is a viewer bug, source-PDF page-label issue, or user-facing mapping confusion.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The relevant document is identified or the bead records that it is missing locally
- [ ] The 1063/1073 discrepancy is reproduced or ruled out
- [ ] The likely cause is documented
- [ ] A follow-up implementation bead is created if there is a general viewer bug

## Verification

Use the real cached/local KTN document and compare viewer page, printed page label, outline/search result, and browser find behavior for "Internet".

title: Explore visual block mode for PDF text selection
description:
## Context

The user is curious about a visual block mode. This is exploratory and should not be implemented as a full feature until the interaction model is clearly useful.

## What to build

Define a small experiment for rectangular/block-style selection in converted PDFs, including what problem it solves better than current visual mode. Do not ship a broad implementation without user review.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A concrete use case is written down
- [ ] The experiment defines commands and visual feedback
- [ ] The user approves whether this is worth implementing
- [ ] Follow-up implementation beads are created only after approval

User reviews the proposed visual block mode interaction and either accepts, rejects, or parks it.

title: Redesign Command-Shift-Period surface as an information bar
description:
## Context

The current Command-Shift-Period UI is a tiny white bubble that stands out. The user mentioned an entire bar with document information, but also said this is out of scope for now and needs visual design thought.

## What to build

Create a design proposal for replacing the bubble with a quiet full-width or header-like bar that can include document information. Do not implement until the design is accepted.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The proposal explains what information belongs in the bar
- [ ] The proposal includes interaction states and when the bar appears/disappears
- [ ] The visual direction is consistent with the viewer style
- [ ] User review decides whether to implement

## Verification

User reviews the design proposal or mockup and decides whether this becomes an implementation bead.

title: Document PDF producer compatibility: xelatex vs pdflatex
description:
## Context

The user observes that xelatex-generated PDFs produce much better selectable text in the viewer, while pdflatex reports can look blurry or OCR-like. This may matter for future pdf2htmlEX integration or input guidance.

## What to build

Investigate a small set of xelatex and pdflatex PDFs, document which PDF features affect pdf2htmlEX extraction/rendering quality, and capture practical guidance for source PDFs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Compare at least one xelatex and one pdflatex generated PDF if examples are available
- [ ] Identify whether the difference is fonts, embedded text, images, encoding, or another PDF feature
- [ ] Document practical guidance for producing viewer-friendly PDFs
- [ ] Create future engine-level beads if deeper pdf2htmlEX changes are warranted

## Verification

Run both sample PDFs through the viewer and compare selectable text, rendered clarity, and extracted DOM text.

title: Park future pdf2htmlEX, Vimium, and native app integration tracks
description:

The notes mention integrating with/forking pdf2htmlEX, rewriting it for arm64, forking Vimium, and eventually shipping a monolithic macOS menu bar app. The user explicitly framed these as future/out-of-scope for the current LLM-driven development pass.

title: Fix light HTML resolution, selection, and search before rollout
description:
## Context

The experimental low-memory light HTML variant reduces browser memory substantially, but the user tested AlgDat in the in-app browser and found three blocking regressions:

- Page image resolution is visibly too low/blurry at reading zoom.
- Text selection is botched/misaligned and selects huge/coarse transparent text regions.
- Native search does not work acceptably in real browser use, despite the earlier synthetic window.find proof.

This means pdfv-yg1.17 is not actually done. The light format must remain experimental and must not be bulk-applied to existing cached PDFs until these issues are fixed.

## What to build

Redesign or replace the light variant so it keeps the memory win without degrading the core reader contract. Investigate at least:

- whether rasters are low because of source extraction, CSS zoom scaling, image intrinsic size, or pdf2htmlEX output resolution;
- whether selection/search need line-level text rather than page-level text, or a separate hidden search layer plus canonical selection layer;
- whether a hybrid mode can keep exact visible text for nearby pages and cheap searchable text for far pages.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AlgDat light/test variant renders text sharply at normal and zoomed reading sizes
- [ ] Drag/Vimium selection is line-aligned enough for real reading/copying
- [ ] Native Cmd-F works in the actual browser UI, not only via window.find
- [ ] Memory remains meaningfully below canonical on the 1677-page AlgDat book
- [ ] Bulk light generation remains disabled until all above pass
- [ ] docs/cache.md and ADR 0010 reflect the final accepted tradeoff

## Verification

Use the in-app browser or Comet on the AlgDat link. Verify visual sharpness, selection, and Cmd-F manually with screenshots if useful. Then compare renderer memory with footprint -p <renderer> -summary against canonical and the fixed light variant.

description:
## Context

## What to build

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Opening a converted PDF directly to a non-first-page restored position shows the correct page without requiring movement
- [ ] Opening at the first page still shows page 1
- [ ] The fix works with normal reload and hard reload
- [ ] No page-position cache is trusted until the DOM has enough information to compute current visibility

title: Stop Tab from changing pages
description:
## Context

Pressing Tab currently changes pages. The user does not want Tab to be a page navigation command in the viewer. Tab should preserve normal focus traversal or be safely ignored depending on the active surface.

## What to build

Find the Tab handler or browser-default interaction that causes page changes and remove that behavior without breaking semantic focus for overlay controls.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pressing Tab in the document surface does not move to another page
- [ ] Pressing Tab inside menus/dialogs still follows useful focus behavior or is intentionally scoped
- [ ] docs/keybindings.md is updated if Tab is currently documented as a command

## Verification

Open a converted PDF, note the current page, press Tab repeatedly in the document surface, and verify the page does not change.

title: Prevent dragging the PDF background image while selecting text
description:
## Context

pdf2htmlEX leaves image/background layers behind the text. When the user starts near text but misses and hits the background, Chrome can drag the page image instead of behaving like a PDF text viewer.

## What to build

Make non-text PDF background/image layers non-draggable and non-interactive where appropriate, while preserving text selection and links.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Dragging on page whitespace or background does not start a browser image drag ghost
- [ ] Text can still be selected normally
- [ ] Links or intentional clickable elements still work
- [ ] The change is scoped to converted PDF page layers, not global browser behavior

## Verification

In a converted PDF, drag from whitespace near text and confirm no image drag starts; then select real text and click a real link if available.

title: Stop text selection from snapping to the top when dragged into whitespace
description:
## Context

When selecting text, moving the cursor into whitespace can cause the selection to extend unexpectedly up to the top of the page. The desired behavior is closer to a normal PDF/text viewer: missing text should not explode the selection range.

## What to build

Diagnose the text-layer geometry or selection event behavior that causes whitespace drags to anchor incorrectly, then constrain selection behavior so whitespace does not select unrelated earlier page text.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A repro case demonstrates the current whitespace-to-top selection jump
- [ ] Dragging slightly outside text no longer selects unrelated text at the top of the page
- [ ] Normal multi-line text selection still works
- [ ] The fix does not disable native text selection globally

## Verification

On a representative converted PDF, drag-select a sentence/paragraph and move the pointer into nearby whitespace; confirm the selection remains local.

title: Make copied/visible selections preserve spaces between words
description:
## Context

Selections can look or behave as if they are chopped at spaces. The underlying text segmentation may be necessary for browser find, but the user-facing selection/copy experience should preserve normal word spacing.

## What to build

Investigate whether the chopped selection is visual, clipboard text, DOM text segmentation, or CSS spacing. Improve the selection/copy surface so selected sentences behave as continuous text with spaces.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reproduce a selection where spaces cause visibly or clipboard-chopped output
- [ ] Selected/copied text preserves spaces between words
- [ ] Native Cmd-F behavior is not regressed
- [ ] The change is documented if it relies on pdf2htmlEX DOM quirks

## Verification

Select and copy a sentence with spaces from a converted PDF, paste it into a plain text field, and verify normal spacing.

title: Prevent stale native-find selection from jumping the viewport back
description:
## Context

The overlay has custom selection-following behavior for marked/selected text. After native Cmd-F selects text, later scrolling and pressing Enter can reselect the old find result and jump the document back to that old location.

## What to build

Separate intentional overlay-driven selection movement from stale native browser find selection. The viewer should not unexpectedly jump back to an old find selection when the user is trying to continue reading or selecting elsewhere.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reproduce the stale Cmd-F selection jump
- [ ] Pressing Enter after scrolling away does not resurrect an old find selection unless the browser find UI is actively being used
- [ ] Existing intentional selection auto-scroll behavior still works for active visual/mark workflows
- [ ] The boundary between native find and overlay selection handling is clear in code comments or docs if non-obvious

## Verification

Use Cmd-F to find text, scroll away, interact with selection/navigation, press Enter, and confirm the viewport does not jump back unexpectedly.
